subject: Multi-track acceptance roadmap — SOC 2 / Audit logs / Retention (post-call)
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Hoffman <lena@finbridge.io>, security@finbridge.io
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Multi-track acceptance roadmap — SOC 2 / Audit logs / Retention (post-call)

Thanks for the call earlier — great to meet you and the FinBridge security team. Quick written recap so we have a single place to track owners and next steps. High-level from today's discussion: 

Summary of pain & goals:
- FinBridge needs a formal acceptance path for Redwood inference for production in mid-Q2 (target: 2028-05-15).
- Primary gating items: SOC 2 report (Type II preferred), 90–180 day audit-log samples, DPA with a few retention clarifications, and a pen-test window.
- Minimal latency/observability concerns handled separately — this thread focused on security evidence.

What Redwood will provide (proposed):
- SOC 2 summary + control mapping (redacted where needed). (Owner: Mateo)
- Sample audit logs (time-windowed CSV + description of fields) and a short guide on retention/archival options. (Owner: Irene)
- A DPA redline for your legal team to review; we can accept a single redline pass and then escalate for legal sign-off. (Owner: Marissa)
- Proposed pen-test window and scope template. (Owner: Mateo/Irene)

Your asks / constraints you called out:
- You need an extract of audit logs with the event types: request_id, timestamp, model_id, route, token_count, requester_id, response_time.
- Retention question: can Redwood support a 365-day retention export for audit purposes? Also asked about retention exceptions and data subject access timelines.
- DPA: FinBridge legal prefers trackable redlines and a comment on subprocessor list.

Immediate next steps (proposed timeline):
1) Redwood: send SOC 2 summary + control mapping by 2028-03-09. (Mateo)
2) FinBridge: confirm whether S3 upload or secure sharepoint is preferred for log samples by 2028-03-07. (Lena/Tom)
3) Redwood: provide audit-log sample (anonymized) and log schema by 2028-03-12. (Irene)
4) Marissa to send DPA redline v3 by 2028-03-08; iterate as needed. (Marissa)
5) Agree pen-test week (target w/c 2028-04-23) and define scope. (Irene/Mateo)

Attachments: redwood-call-notes-20280305.txt (call notes), we will follow with the SOC 2 summary and a short artifact checklist.

If the timeline above looks reasonable please reply with confirmations or adjustments — I summarized owners inline to avoid back-and-forth.

Thanks again — excited to move this forward.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0193

Subject: Re: Multi-track acceptance roadmap — SOC 2 / Audit logs / Retention (post-call)

Thanks, Mateo — useful summary. Confirming a few items from our side: 

1) Upload method: secure S3 upload is preferred (we’ll provide temporary creds + a short manifest).
2) For SOC 2, if you can provide: report summary, auditor name, and control mapping (trust services criteria -> Redwood control), that will let our compliance team evaluate quickly. Full report is fine under an NDA if needed.
3) Log sample: we can accept an anonymized CSV; our reviewers want at least 90 days of representative activity (not necessarily continuous). We can accept compressed samples.
4) Retention: ideally we want to confirm whether Redwood can perform on-demand exports up to 365 days. If that requires special handling or an additional package, flag that now.
5) Pen-test: we prefer a 7–10 day testing window, with agreed scope and blackout times. Our pen-test vendor needs a baseline network diagram and a point of contact for any urgent issues.

Attaching our log schema for reference: finbridge-log-schema.csv (contains the event fields we look for).

We’ll coordinate internally on precise dates and reply by EOD Wednesday with the S3 details.

-Lena
Lena Hoffman
Head of Security, FinBridge
lena@finbridge.io

Thanks Lena — copying a more technical response and a few clarifications from our side.

Quick answers:
- 365-day exports: Redwood supports exports up to 365 days, but full production exports at that range require a short lead (2–3 business days) to assemble and redact PII per your guidance.
- Anonymized audit sample: we will provide a gzipped CSV that follows your schema (we’ll drop requester_email and replace with requester_id hashes).
- Upload: S3 presigned URLs are fine; we’ll accept either an S3 bucket where you push or Redwood can push to a FinBridge bucket if you prefer (we’ll need write creds).
- Pen-test scope: proposed scope attached inline in the body below (short). We can support a 7-day window w/ one on-call engineering contact + a channel to our security team.

Technical acceptance thresholds (our suggested minimal checks):
- Logs: include request_id, timestamp (ISO8601), model_id, route, requester_id (hashed), token_count, response_time_ms, status_code. Provide sample size >= 5,000 lines across 90 days to show distribution.
- SOC 2: provide Type II attestation and a control mapping CSV (we’ll redact specific test artifacts).
- DPA: Redwood’s legal team prefers to keep retention language consistent with our current customers; Marissa will share redline.

We can own the audit-log sample and SOC 2 summary delivery dates: audit sample by 2028-03-12, SOC2 summary by 2028-03-09. I’ll also prepare an internal evidence-handoff checklist and share it in the next update.

Pen-test scope (short): external blackbox for inference endpoints only; no DoS tests; no social engineering; agreed window and test IP list to be exchanged one week before.

If that aligns, I’ll schedule the pen-test planning call for the week of 2028-03-20.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Security Solutions, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai
